response.outreach_email:
Subject: Question about your work as a startup PM

Hi Jo,

I'm Kim Alvarez, an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028. Before the program, I worked as an analyst from 2023 to 2026. I'm trying to understand how product management works in practice, and I'd value hearing about your experience as a PM at a startup: how you spend your time, how you decide what to prioritize, and how you came into the role.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call or coffee in the coming weeks? I'm happy to work around your schedule.

Thank you,
Kim Alvarez
questions: What does a typical week look like for you as a PM at your startup, and how much of your time goes to customers, engineering, and strategy?
At a startup, where resources are limited, how do you decide what gets built next when several priorities compete?
How did you come into a PM role at a startup, and what made that setting the right fit for you?
Which skills have mattered most in your PM work, and which ones did you have to build on the job?
For someone coming from an analyst role, which habits carry over well to startup product management, and which ones would I need to unlearn?

tmay_2min.text: Thank you for taking the time to meet with me, Jo. I appreciate it, and I'll keep my introduction brief so we have plenty of time for your perspective.
My name is Kim Alvarez, and I'm an MBA candidate in the Class of 2028.
Before starting the program, I worked as an analyst from 2023 to 2026.

Looking back, what I value most from that period is the discipline it built. Analyst work rewards structured thinking: taking an ambiguous question, breaking it into manageable pieces, being careful with the details, and then presenting a conclusion clearly enough that others can act on it. Those are habits I want to keep developing.

Business school has given me a chance to step back and think deliberately about what comes next. Rather than choosing a direction based on titles or job descriptions, I'm trying to understand how roles work in practice, which is why conversations like this one are so valuable to me.
You're a PM at a startup,

and that combination is one I'd like to understand better. My impression is that product management at a startup can look quite different from the same title at a larger organization, with fewer layers, faster decisions, and a wider range of responsibilities. I'd value hearing how that matches your experience.

In particular, I'm interested in how you spend your time across a typical week, how you decide what to prioritize when everything feels urgent, and which skills have mattered most in your role. I'd also like to hear how you found your way to it.
I'm still early in figuring out my own path, so I'm here mainly to listen and learn.
